name: Plant-Disease-Detection
description: The Plant-Disease-Detection dataset contains images of plant leaves with disease symptoms, paired with a textual detection prompt. Models must localize and classify diseased regions by predicting bounding boxes with disease class labels.
card_text: This dataset is a visual object detection benchmark for plant disease diagnosis. Each sample consists of a single image of a plant leaf (or plant part) showing disease symptoms, a short textual prompt that instructs the model to identify and localize the disease, and a target annotation in the form of bounding boxes. Each bounding box is a dictionary mapping a disease class name (such as Tomato_Blight or Strawberry_Gray_Mold) to four coordinates [x, y, width, height] specifying the affected region. The images are photographs captured under field-like conditions, focusing on a single leaf or lesion. The dataset assumes the model can interpret visual symptoms and output spatial localizations; the prompt is a generic placeholder for user-defined instructions. It is suitable for evaluating detection and localization capabilities in agricultural contexts.

image.semantics: Path to a photograph of a plant leaf exhibiting disease symptoms. This image is the primary visual input, and the bounding boxes in the output refer to regions within it.

question.semantics: A user-defined prompt that instructs the model to detect and localize plant diseases in the provided image. It provides the task instruction but contains no disease-specific content.

bbox.semantics: A list of bounding box annotations. Each item maps a plant disease category (e.g., Tomato_Blight, Strawberry_Gray_Mold) to coordinates [x, y, width, height] that localize the diseased region in the input image. This is the target output for detection and localization.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample contains an image path, a text prompt, and bounding box annotations. The image is the visual input showing a plant leaf with disease symptoms. The prompt is a generic instruction to detect and localize diseases. The output bbox is a list of dictionaries, each pairing a disease class name with four coordinates that specify the location of the diseased region in the image.
